q: What do we know about feat-txc-normalise-v2 in the txn-categorization project?
a: It strips store numbers, hash codes and city suffixes from merchant descriptors before tokenising (built 2025-09-22). It lifted txc-gbm-v2 macro-F1 from 0.78 to 0.81 on holdout-2025q2 (exp-104) and is part of txc-gbm-v3.

q: What came of exp-106 in the txn-categorization project?
a: exp-106 showed merchant-history features scoring 0.91 macro-F1 on a random split but only 0.78 on a time split (0.77 without history). That led to fnd-txc-history-leaks: history features were dropped from txc-gbm-v3.

q: What does txc-gbm-v3 use as inputs in the txn-categorization project?
a: feat-txc-descriptor-tokens-v2 (char and word tokens on normalised descriptors), feat-txc-normalise-v2 and feat-txc-mcc-prior. It does not use feat-txc-merchant-history-v1.

q: What is the current merchant categorisation model in the txn-categorization project?
a: txc-gbm-v3, a LightGBM model adopted in March 2026 that supersedes txc-gbm-v2 in the nightly insights run. The char-CNN and logistic baseline are not in use.

q: What macro-F1 does txc-gbm-v3 score on txc-oot-2026h1 in the txn-categorization project?
a: 0.83 macro-F1 on txc-oot-2026h1 (3,100 merchants, time-based split). The normalisation step alone gave 0.81 on holdout-2025q2 (exp-104).

q: Why was the char-CNN not shipped in the txn-categorization project?
a: It reached macro-F1 0.80 on holdout-2025q2, but its p95 latency was 210 ms per 1,000 merchants versus 9 ms for LightGBM, and its 0.02 gain over txc-gbm-v2 did not justify a second model stack.
